entries.headline: ArgoCDTools README says the argocd-hook image's Terraform is unpinned; the Dockerfile pins 1.16.3
body: ArgoCDTools README.md:155 lists the image's Terraform as 'unpinned from the HashiCorp noble suite, as the iac image installs it'. argocd-hook/Dockerfile sets TERRAFORM_VERSION=1.16.3 and installs terraform=${TERRAFORM_VERSION}-1, and its comment says the version is pinned identically in three images and bumped together (AnsibleSpecs decisions.md, 'Terraform version'). The session's grounding G1 already flagged the line as stale. No phase of this slice edits it.
entries.consequence: A reader of the ArgoCDTools README is told that a rebuild of the hook image picks up whatever Terraform the suite serves, when it is pinned and must be bumped together with iac and kube-coder-iac-toolchain.
entries.proposal: fix now — one line in README.md:155, saying 'pinned (TERRAFORM_VERSION), bumped with the other two images'.
entries.author: plan-writer r1, planning, ArgoCDTools README.md:155 against argocd-hook/Dockerfile

entries.headline: Settle V10 after the operator's APPLY=true build of IaC/Destroy Stage against …
body: V10 — The operator's `APPLY=true` build against FieldnotesDeploy `dev` leaves the RBD image `fieldnotes-dev-data`, the PV `fieldnotes-dev-data-pv` and `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/` in TerraformState gone, and `config/dev/` deleted from FieldnotesDeploy (ANS-147's done-when).

`verification.json` marks V10 owed after: the operator's APPLY=true build of IaC/Destroy Stage against FieldnotesDeploy dev (Ruling D3). The run cannot take that action; settle the criterion once it has happened.
entries.consequence: V10 stays unproven until then; the test phase does not settle it.
entries.proposal: When that has happened, say so: the session settles V10 in verification.json.

entries.headline: JenkinsDeploy: the controller's jenkins-admin ClusterRole grants every verb on every core resource cluster-wide, Secrets included
body: Live on prd, ClusterRole `jenkins-admin` is `[{apiGroups: [""], resources: ["*"], verbs: ["*"]}]`, bound by ClusterRoleBinding `jenkins-admin` to `jenkins-prd/jenkins-admin`, the controller's ServiceAccount (JenkinsDeploy `chart/templates/jenkins-clusterrole.yaml`, `jenkins-deployment.yaml:28`). It reads every Secret in the cluster (`argocd-hook-credentials` in `argocd-hooks`, Argo's repo credential and OIDC client secret in `argocd-prd`) and creates pods in any namespace. argo-cd D1 says Jenkins holds no cluster credential, and D33/D41 bind the hook credentials to Argo's sync; Ruling Q1 overruled them narrowly for one dedicated identity, which reaches less than the controller already does. Seen while writing D66 in P1; the register says nothing about it. What the Kubernetes plugin actually needs (pods, pods/exec, pods/log in jenkins-prd, perhaps more) is not established.
entries.consequence: Code execution in the Jenkins controller (an admin's script console, a compromised plugin) reads every Secret in the cluster, the hook's credentials among them, while the argo-cd register states that Jenkins holds no cluster credential.
entries.proposal: card — scope the controller's role to what the Kubernetes plugin needs; a security change that needs its own proof across every pipeline, not this slice's.
entries.author: code-writer, P1, r1 — kubectl --context prd get clusterrole/clusterrolebinding jenkins-admin; JenkinsDeploy f3ee7df chart/templates/jenkins-clusterrole.yaml

entries.headline: Keep the Destroy Stage ServiceAccount's exclusivity a convention, or enforce it?
body: In effect, and recorded in D66 and D41 as amended (P1): only `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage`'s pod spec names the dedicated ServiceAccount in `jenkins-prd` (Ruling D1), and nothing enforces that. prd has no ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and no webhook that checks `serviceAccountName` (only the cnpg, ESO and metallb webhooks), so any Jenkinsfile's pod spec can name it, and `jenkins-prd/default` can create Jobs in `jenkins-prd` (Role `jenkins-agent-jobs`) whose pods name it. Holding it means creating Jobs in `argocd-hooks` under `tf-presync` with `argocd-hook-credentials`.
- Keep the convention (in effect): costs nothing; whoever writes a Jenkinsfile in the estate can reach the hook's credentials.

- Enforce in the cluster: a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy in `jenkins-prd` that admits the ServiceAccount only on pods carrying something the pipeline alone sets. Nothing a Jenkinsfile cannot also set exists today, so this takes design, a JenkinsDeploy change and a test.
- Enforce in Jenkins: a Kubernetes cloud or pod-template restriction that only this job may use. Design in JenkinsDeploy's controller configuration.
entries.consequence: Write access to any Jenkinsfile in the estate reaches the hook's whole credential set through that ServiceAccount, which Ruling D1 meant to keep to one pipeline.
entries.proposal: keep — every Jenkinsfile that could name it lives in the operator's own repos, and the controller's jenkins-admin ClusterRole already reaches further; revisit with that defect's card.
entries.author: code-writer, P1, r1 — kubectl --context prd get validatingadmissionpolicies / validatingwebhookconfigurations; JenkinsDeploy chart/templates/jenkins-agent-jobs-role.yaml
